ov: Very large rays with a long, flat snout lined with teeth like a saw. They live in warm coastal seas, estuaries and even rivers and lakes, and use the saw to find and strike fish. All five species are critically endangered, with strongholds left only in northern Australia and Florida.

why.dg: Docile and generally harmless, but a captured sawfish defending itself can cause serious injuries with its saw.
why.et: Hunted for its fins, used in shark fin soup, and for its teeth and saw in traditional medicine.

rg: Tropical and subtropical coasts, estuaries and rivers worldwide, but now gone from much of that range except northern Australia and Florida.
df: Fish and invertebrates, found and caught with the saw.
fx: Females give birth to live young once a year or every second year.
It can sense prey about 40 cm away from the electric fields the prey gives off.
